title: Latency-aware Model Bundling: GTM Signal Deck & Purchase Trigger Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Synthesize market research and competitive signals into a go-to-market (GTM) deck and tactical playbook recommending bundled model offerings that optimize for latency-sensitive use cases. Deliverables will include a customer-needs segmentation (by latency tolerance and cost sensitivity), a competitive positioning matrix, recommended bundle SKUs (hosted + dedicated options), and a trigger-based purchase guide for sales/solutions teams.
background: Sales and Solutions teams report increasing demand for predictable latency behavior in RAG/assist features. We see customers choosing edge or private deployments when latency tolerance is low, but they are also highly price-sensitive. Competitors are packaging models with latency SLAs or offering pre-bundled low-latency SKUs — we lack an explicit GTM artifact that ties model variants to purchase triggers. This ticket consolidates signals from model landscape tracking, pricing sensitivity interviews, and latency benchmarks into a single actionable playbook.
goals: Create a one-page customer segmentation tied to latency buckets (<50ms, 50-150ms, 150-500ms, >500ms) and economic tolerance
Produce a competitive matrix that maps vendor bundling behaviors and SLA offerings
Recommend 3 product bundle prototypes (self-serve hosted, reserved Dedicated, Private-lift) with suggested pricing and technical constraints
Produce a short purchase-trigger playbook for AEs and Solutions to surface the right bundle during discovery
deliverables: GTM slide deck (12-15 slides) -- Confluence + Google Slides link included
One-page purchase trigger cheat-sheet for sellers
Bundle SKU spec doc (model variants, expected p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens)
Customer interview summary (10 interviews) and raw notes
acceptance_criteria: Deck reviewed and approved by GTM lead and Head of Product
Bundle specs validated with infra/serving lead (latency feasibility confirmed)
Sales playbook accepted by 2 pilot AE teams and used in at least 5 discovery calls
Benchmarks attached show median p95 latency estimates within 20% of projections for recommended bundles
tasks: Compile competitor packaging data (pricing tiers, SLAs, bundling) — responsible: Marco
Run targeted latency-cost microbenchmarks for candidate model variants (50/100/200 token sequences) — dependency: ENG-1987
Conduct 10 customer interviews to validate purchase triggers — responsible: Lina (Customer Research)
Draft GTM slides and cheat-sheet; iterate with Sales and Solutions — responsible: PM team
Finalize bundle SKU spec and create support ticket for catalog rollout (ENG & Billing coordination)
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff 1: Offer narrower high-cost low-latency bundles vs broad mid-tier bundles. Recommendation is 2 narrow low-latency SKUs + 1 mid-tier to avoid fragmenting inventory.
Tradeoff 2: Guaranteeing p99 SLA for hosted is expensive; propose a best-effort SLA with optional paid SLA add-on for dedicated customers.
Decision: Do not include extreme on-prem latency guarantees in initial bundles; route Private offers through a separate enterprise procurement flow.
risks: Benchmarks may not generalize across customer workload distributions — mitigate by including margin buffers and running appeared-customer synthetic workloads
Competitive pricing moves could invalidate suggested SKUs quickly — include monitoring recipe for monthly refresh
Billing + product_catalog release timelines could delay availability of bundles — add dependency with ENG and Billing teams
